**WorldView 3 Mosaicking, and Cloud Masking**

This script mosaics multiple WorldView-3 satellite scenes into a single image and applies cloud and shadow masking to prepare the data for further analysis.

The workflow begins by loading the required packages.

```{r}
#| label: Packages

library(terra)
library(sf)
library(reticulate) # provides an R interface to Python modules, classes, and functions.
library(RStoolbox)

```

WorldView-3 data are provided as a series of .tif files. In this workflow, multispectral images for each month are mosaicked into a single composite image, and panchromatic images for each month are similarly mosaicked into a single file. The WorldView-3 scenes, including both multispectral and panchromatic bands, are then imported into R for further processing.

```{r}
#| labbel: image-scenes

# set the working directory

setwd("C:/Users/cp844/University of Exeter/TESSLab - Chafika Phiri Data/Objective 3 Manuscript/Satellite Data")

# kremetart scenes with multispectral bands collected on July 22, 2024.

krem_ms_july_files <- list.files(
  "Data/050333425010_01_Kre/050333425010_01_P001_MUL",
  pattern = "\\.tif$",
  full.names = TRUE,
  ignore.case = TRUE
)

krem_pan_july_files <- list.files(
  "Data/050333425010_01_Kre/050333425010_01_P001_PAN",
  pattern = "\\.tif$",
  full.names = TRUE,
  ignore.case = TRUE  
)

krem_ms_feb_files <- list.files(
  "Data/050333425010_01_Kre/050333425010_01_P002_MUL",
  pattern = "\\.tif$",
  full.names = TRUE,
  ignore.case = TRUE  
)

krem_pan_feb_files <- list.files(
  "Data/050333425010_01_Kre/050333425010_01_P002_PAN",
  pattern = "\\.tif$",
  full.names = TRUE,
  ignore.case = TRUE  
)

# mapungubwe scenes

maps_ms_july_files <- list.files("Data/050333425020_01_Maps/050333974010_01_P001_MUL",
  pattern = "\\.tif$",
  full.names = TRUE,
  ignore.case = TRUE
)

maps_pan_july_files <- list.files("Data/050333425020_01_Maps/050333974010_01_P001_PAN",
  pattern = "\\.tif$",
  full.names = TRUE,
  ignore.case = TRUE  
)

# Load each multispectral band as a list of SpatRaster objects

krem_ms_july_spatraster <- sprc(krem_ms_july_files)
krem_pan_july_spatraster <- sprc(krem_pan_july_files)
krem_ms_feb_spatraster <- sprc(krem_ms_feb_files)
krem_pan_feb_spatraster <- sprc(krem_pan_feb_files)
maps_ms_july_spatraster <- sprc(maps_ms_july_files)
maps_pan_july_spatraster <- sprc(maps_pan_july_files)

# mosaic the spatraster to generate a single image for each month and sensor

krem_ms_july_mosaic <- terra::mosaic(krem_ms_july_spatraster)
krem_pan_july_mosaic <- terra::mosaic(krem_pan_july_spatraster)
krem_ms_feb_mosaic <- terra::mosaic(krem_ms_feb_spatraster)
krem_pan_feb_mosaic <- terra::mosaic(krem_pan_feb_spatraster)
maps_ms_july_mosaic <- terra::mosaic(maps_ms_july_spatraster)
maps_pan_july_mosaic <- terra::mosaic(maps_pan_july_spatraster)

# save all the mosaicked images

writeRaster(krem_ms_july_mosaic, "Data/Mosaicked_Images/Kremetart/krem_ms_july_mosaic.tiff", overwrite = TRUE)

writeRaster(krem_pan_july_mosaic, "Data/Mosaicked_Images/Kremetart/krem_pan_july_mosaic.tiff", overwrite = TRUE)

writeRaster(krem_ms_feb_mosaic, "Data/Mosaicked_Images/Kremetart/krem_ms_feb_mosaic.tiff", overwrite = TRUE)

writeRaster(krem_pan_feb_mosaic, "Data/Mosaicked_Images/Kremetart/krem_pan_feb_mosaic.tiff", overwrite = TRUE)


writeRaster(maps_ms_july_mosaic, "Data/Mosaicked_Images/Mapungubwe/maps_ms_july_mosaic.tiff", overwrite = TRUE)

writeRaster(maps_pan_july_mosaic, "Data/Mosaicked_Images/Mapungubwe/maps_pan_july_mosaic.tiff", overwrite = TRUE)

```

**Image-to-image co-registration** This sections performs image co-registration of WorldView-3 multispectral imagery from Kremetart, South Africa \| Target: February \| Reference: July. Method: mutual information (RStoolbox::coregisterImages)

```{r}

# Paths 

base_dir  <- "C:/Users/cp844/University of Exeter/TESSLab - Chafika Phiri Data/Objective 3 Manuscript/Satellite Data/Data"
image_dir <- file.path(base_dir, "Mosaicked_Images", "Kremetart")

target_path <- file.path(image_dir, "krem_ms_feb_mosaic.tiff")   # image to be moved
ref_path    <- file.path(image_dir, "krem_ms_july_mosaic.tiff")  # image held fixed
out_path    <- file.path(image_dir, "krem_ms_feb_mosaic_coregistered.tif")

stopifnot(file.exists(target_path), file.exists(ref_path))  # fail early if missing

# Load imagery 
krem_target <- terra::rast(target_path)  # February
krem_ref    <- terra::rast(ref_path)     # July

# Validate geometry 
# Mutual information compares pixel pairs, so both images must share a CRS and
# an identical pixel size, otherwise the shift search is meaningless.
stopifnot(
  terra::same.crs(krem_target, krem_ref),
  all(abs(terra::res(krem_target) - terra::res(krem_ref)) < 1e-6)
)

# Choose a single band for the shift search 
# One band is sufficient to estimate a linear x-y shift and is far faster than
# eight. The NIR1 band (WV-3 band 7) gives strong vegetation contrast.
search_band <- 7

target_band <- krem_target[[search_band]]
ref_band    <- krem_ref[[search_band]]

# Restrict the search to the common overlap 
# Non-overlapping margins contribute no shared information and slow the search.
overlap     <- terra::intersect(terra::ext(target_band), terra::ext(ref_band))
target_band <- terra::crop(target_band, overlap)
ref_band    <- terra::crop(ref_band,    overlap)

# Replace NA with 0 (search copies only) 
# The algorithm cannot process NA. subst() is memory-safe; the substitution is
# applied to the search copies so that the exported image keeps its true NAs.
target_band <- terra::subst(target_band, NA, 0)
ref_band    <- terra::subst(ref_band,    NA, 0)

# Estimate the optimal shift 
# Tests every shift in seq(-shift, shift, by = shiftInc) in x and y (441 shifts
# here) and retains the one maximising mutual information.
coreg <- RStoolbox::coregisterImages(
  img         = target_band,  # moved
  ref         = ref_band,     # fixed
  shift       = 10,           # maximum search radius, in pixels
  shiftInc    = 1,            # search step, in pixels
  nSamples    = 10000,        # pixels sampled per shift
  nBins       = 100,          # bins of the joint histogram
  reportStats = TRUE,         # return $MI, $bestShift, $jointHist, $coregImg
  verbose     = TRUE
)

best_shift <- coreg$bestShift  # data.frame of the optimal x and y shift, in pixels
print(best_shift)

# Warn if the optimum sits on the edge of the search window: the true optimum
# may lie beyond it, in which case `shift` should be increased.
if (max(abs(unlist(best_shift[, c("x", "y")]))) >= 10) {
  warning("Optimal shift reached the search limit; increase `shift` and re-run.")
}

# Apply the shift to the full multispectral stack 
# coreg$coregImg holds the corrected single band only, so the estimated shift is
# converted from pixels to map units and applied to all bands of the original.
dx_m <- best_shift$x * terra::xres(krem_target)
dy_m <- best_shift$y * terra::yres(krem_target)

krem_feb_aligned <- terra::shift(krem_target, dx = dx_m, dy = dy_m)

# Visual check
# Plot the two images side by side over the shared extent; overplotting with
# add = TRUE simply hides the lower image and shows nothing useful.
op <- par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
terra::plotRGB(terra::crop(krem_ref, overlap),
               r = 5, g = 3, b = 2, stretch = "lin", main = "July (reference)")
terra::plotRGB(terra::crop(krem_feb_aligned, overlap),
               r = 5, g = 3, b = 2, stretch = "lin", main = "February (aligned)")
par(op)

# Export 
terra::writeRaster(
  krem_feb_aligned,
  filename  = out_path,
  datatype  = "INT2U",                          # WV-3 digital numbers are 16-bit
  gdal      = c("COMPRESS=LZW", "TILED=YES"),
  overwrite = TRUE
)

```

**Cloud and shadow masking**

Cloud and shadow masking is performed using the OmnicloudMask model. As the model is implemented in Python, the reticulate package is used to interface Python within the R environment.

The OmnicloudMask model was trained on Sentinel-2 imagery with a spatial resolution of 10 m. To ensure compatibility, the higher-resolution WorldView-3 imagery (0.3 m) is resampled to 10 m prior to inference.

```{python}

# cloud_mask.py -- OmniCloudMask cloud and shadow masking for WorldView-3

from pathlib import Path                      # object-oriented file paths
import numpy as np
import rasterio as rio
from rasterio.enums import Resampling         # resampling algorithms (average, nearest, ...)
from rasterio.warp import reproject           # regrids an array between two transforms
from scipy.ndimage import binary_dilation     # morphological buffering of the mask
from omnicloudmask import predict_from_array

# --- set up -----------------------------------------------------------
base_folder = Path(
    "C:/Users/cp844/University of Exeter/TESSLab - Chafika Phiri Data/"
    "Objective 3 Manuscript/Satellite Data"
)
image_path = base_folder / "Data/Mosaicked_Images/Kremetart/krem_ms_feb_mosaic_coregistered.tif"
mask_path   = image_path.with_name(image_path.stem + "_cloudmask10m.tif")
masked_path = image_path.with_name(image_path.stem + "_masked.tif")

target_resolution = 10        # metres: the resolution OmniCloudMask expects
red_green_nir     = [5, 3, 7] # WorldView-3 Red, Green, NIR1 -- the order the model requires
buffer_pixels     = 2         # dilate by 2 coarse pixels = 20 m

# --- Read and resample to 10 m ----------------------------------------------
with rio.open(image_path) as source:
    if source.count != 8:
        raise ValueError(f"Expected 8 bands, found {source.count}.")

    scale = source.res[0] / target_resolution     # derived from the file, so this works
    coarse_height = max(1, round(source.height * scale))   # for the 1.2 m multispectral
    coarse_width  = max(1, round(source.width  * scale))   # mosaic as well as the 0.3 m product

    coarse_array = source.read(
        red_green_nir,
        out_shape=(3, coarse_height, coarse_width),
        resampling=Resampling.average             # radiometric averaging, not nearest neighbour
    ).astype(np.float32)

    coarse_transform = source.transform * source.transform.scale(
        source.width / coarse_width,
        source.height / coarse_height
    )
    source_profile = source.profile.copy()

# --- Inference ---------------------------------------------------------------
mask = predict_from_array(
    coarse_array,
    no_data_value=0,
    apply_no_data_mask=True
)
mask = mask[0].astype(np.uint8)   # (1, h, w) -> (h, w); 0=Clear 1=Thick 2=Thin 3=Shadow

# --- Buffer cloud and shadow -------------------------------------------------
contaminated = binary_dilation(
    mask != 0,
    structure=np.ones((3, 3), dtype=bool),
    iterations=buffer_pixels
)

# --- Write the 10 m four-class mask -----------------------------------------
mask_profile = source_profile.copy()
mask_profile.update(
    driver="GTiff", dtype="uint8", count=1, nodata=255,
    height=coarse_height, width=coarse_width,
    transform=coarse_transform, compress="deflate"
)
with rio.open(mask_path, "w", **mask_profile) as destination:
    destination.write(mask, 1)

# --- Apply the mask at full resolution, block by block -----------------------
with rio.open(image_path) as source:
    mask_full = np.zeros((source.height, source.width), dtype=np.uint8)
    reproject(
        source=contaminated.astype(np.uint8), destination=mask_full,
        src_transform=coarse_transform, dst_transform=source.transform,
        src_crs=source.crs, dst_crs=source.crs,
        resampling=Resampling.nearest             # categorical data: nearest only
    )

    output_profile = source.profile.copy()
    output_profile.update(nodata=0, compress="deflate", tiled=True, BIGTIFF="IF_SAFER")

    with rio.open(masked_path, "w", **output_profile) as destination:
        for _, window in source.block_windows(1):
            block = source.read(window=window)
            rows = slice(window.row_off, window.row_off + window.height)
            cols = slice(window.col_off, window.col_off + window.width)
            block[:, mask_full[rows, cols] == 1] = 0
            destination.write(block, window=window)

# --- Report ------------------------------------------------------------------
total = mask.size
for code, label in enumerate(["Clear", "Thick cloud", "Thin cloud", "Cloud shadow"]):
    print(f"{label:<14}: {100 * (mask == code).sum() / total:.2f}%")
print(f"Mask written to   : {mask_path}")
print(f"Masked image      : {masked_path}")


```

**Pansharpening**

The multispectral mosaics for Kremetart and Mapungubwe were pansharpened using their corresponding panchromatic mosaics in GDAL 3.10.3. Pansharpening was performed using nearest-neighbour resampling through the GDAL command-line utility, which supports multi-band multispectral imagery and can be executed directly for batch processing.
